cards.claim: EMA (Exponential Moving Average) is a weight averaging regularization that helps learn flat optima for better generalization without extra computational cost
cards.evidence: Direct statement of EMA's properties as a weight averaging method
cards.quote: Exponential Moving Average (EMA) is a widely used weight averaging (WA) regularization to learn flat optima for better generalizations without extra cost in deep neural network (DNN) optimization.

cards.claim: Switch EMA (SEMA)—switching EMA parameters back to the original model after each epoch—allows DNNs to reach generalization optima with better flatness-sharpness tradeoff
cards.conditions: Deep neural networks with SEMA modification applied
cards.effect: Improved tradeoff between flatness and sharpness at generalization optima
cards.quote: This work unveils the full potential of EMA with a single line of modification, i.e., switching the EMA parameters to the original model after each epoch, dubbed as Switch EMA (SEMA). From both theoretical and empirical aspects, we demonstrate that SEMA can help DNNs to reach generalization optima that better trade-off between flatness and sharpness.

cards.claim: SEMA improves final performance and convergence speed across diverse tasks without requiring extra test-time computation
cards.conditions: Vision and language tasks: image classification, self-supervised learning, object detection, segmentation, image generation, video prediction, attribute regression, language modeling; with popular optimizers and networks
cards.effect: Performance improvements and faster convergence (magnitude not specified in abstract)
cards.evidence: Comprehensive experimental results across multiple tasks and model types
cards.quote: Comprehensive results with popular optimizers and networks show that SEMA is a free lunch for DNN training by improving performances and boosting convergence speeds.
